newsitem.title: SWEDEN: AssiDoman posts lower than expected profit.
newsitem.headline: AssiDoman posts lower than expected profit.

text.p: Swedish forestry group AssiDoman on Thursday posted a 61 percent slump in 1996 profits, but said it expected a gradual improvement in the business cycle in 1997.
Its profit after financial items plummeted to 1.71 billion crowns against market expectations of 1.95 billion crowns.
AssiDoman said the stronger crown wiped 400 million crowns off operating profit.
"The general market situation remains weak but there are some positive signs within important product areas for AssiDoman, sawn timber, krafliner and board," the company said.
"Order intake is good and prices are stable. A gradual improvement in the business climate is expected in 1997."
AssiDoman reported that operating profit after deprecition dropped 59 precent to 1.84 billion crowns from 4.47 billion crowns in 1995 due to lower prices and a stronger crown.
Fourth quarter operating profit was also charged with 274 million crowns of restructuring costs, primarily deriving from the Packaging and Kraft Products business area, AssiDoman said.
Turnover fell 12 percent ot 19.32 billion crowns.
AssiDoman said pulp prices were expecteed to hit bottom in the first half of 1997.
The weak market situation in 1996 made all business areas, with the exception of Barrier Coating, post lower sales.
The Barrier Coating unit was boosted by the acquisition of the German company PWA-Kunststoff at the end of 1995, the company said.
Fixed capital expenditure fell to 3.91 billion crowns from 6.02 billion in 1995. Of this, 676 million crowns was acquisitions in 1996 and 3.76 billion was acquisitions a year earlier.
Despite falling profits, the company proposed to raise dividend to 5.25 a share, from five crowns, corresponding to 4.0 percent of closing equity, unchanged from last year.
